title: Holding period against the signal's own decay
hypothesis: The 14-day hold came from DS3's two-week horizon in equities, and nothing has tested whether crypto's residual momentum decays on that schedule. If the horizon is wrong the book is either paying to rebalance into a signal that has not moved or holding one that has already gone.

title: Formation window against holding period
hypothesis: Lookback and hold are the two halves of one choice and were never varied together. A 28-day formation feeding a 14-day hold is an assumption inherited twice over, from equity momentum and then from DS3.

title: Does the skip day earn its keep
hypothesis: One day is skipped between formation and holding to avoid the short-horizon reversal that contaminates raw momentum. In crypto the reversal horizon is measured in hours rather than a month, so the skip may be removing signal rather than noise - or may need to be longer.

title: How wide should each leg be
hypothesis: A third of the cross-section per side is a convention from equity portfolio sorts, where the cross-section is thousands of names. On thirty-two names it is ten per leg. A narrower leg concentrates the signal and a wider one diversifies the idiosyncratic risk, and nothing has measured which dominates here.

title: Beta estimation window
hypothesis: Sixty days is the design's declared starting point for the rolling loading and has never been varied. Too short and beta is noise that the residual inherits; too long and it is stale through a regime change, which is exactly when the hedge matters.

title: Seasoning, re-measured against the market factor
hypothesis: The seasoning sweep ran before the market factor was the baseline, so its five values were measured against a book that has since changed underneath them. If 365 days is a genuine threshold it will survive the new baseline; if it was the best of five numbers on the old one, it will not.

title: Does the narrow universe survive the market factor
hypothesis: The only configuration that has ever made money in the sealed year is the fourteen-name book, and it was measured with the BTC factor. Cycles 3 to 5 changed the universe and the factor at once across four sealed reads. Running the narrow universe with the market factor on research years separates the two without spending a fifth.

title: Do the five single-sweep winners add up, or is each one noise
hypothesis: E02, E04, E05 and E06 each found a better value than baseline while varying ONE knob on the same research data. Stacking winners chosen that way is the classic way to manufacture a backtest, so this measures the stack against every single change alone. If the combination is roughly the sum of its parts the effects are real and separable; if it is much better than any part, that is the signature of four selections on one sample rather than of an edge.

title: The narrow universe carried the only positive sealed year - does it take the new formation window
hypothesis: E07 produced the highest risk-adjusted return this system has ever recorded - the fourteen-name universe with the market factor, Sharpe 1.007 and t 2.90 - but only five positive years of eight. Meanwhile the wide book reaches eight of eight and a t of 2.38. Those are two different systems and the choice between them is not obvious. This asks whether the narrow book's consistency problem is fixed by the same three-week formation window that fixed the wide one.

title: Is the three-week formation window a plateau or a spike
hypothesis: Lookback 21 was the only value of six to reach eight positive years out of eight, and its neighbours 14 and 28 both reach seven. A real horizon is a plateau - the values either side of it should be nearly as good - while a spike that its neighbours do not support is the shape of a number that fitted this particular sample. The sweep only tested 14, 21, 42, 56 and 90, so the region around 21 has never actually been looked at.

title: The skip day is load-bearing and nobody expected it to be
hypothesis: E03 is the sharpest result the loop has produced and it was meant to be a routine check. Skipping one day between formation and holding gives a worst year of -2.0%; skipping none gives -27.5%, two gives -31.1% and three gives -40.0%. A one-day window that carries that much of the result is either a real microstructure effect - the short-horizon reversal the skip exists to avoid - or a bug in how the window is offset. This re-runs it against the new baseline to see whether the cliff survives, because a parameter that matters this much deserves more than one measurement.
